title: Rep. Trahan releases updated FRONTIER Act ("2.0") section-by-section (Nov 19): embedded IVO access with government assignment, recursive self-improvement as its own catastrophic-risk category, near-miss reporting and penalties, an Office of AI Security in Commerce
quote_verbatim: Automated AI research and development, including recursive self improvement, is its own category of catastrophic risk.
what_is_new: Changes from FRONTIER 1.0: floor preemption (stronger state laws preserved), government assignment of IVOs, enforceable corrective orders, near-miss penalties and reporting, broader incident reporting with a "should have known" standard; full bill text to follow "in the coming weeks".
why_for_agiright: A federal bill framework on independent evaluation, incident reporting, liability and recursive self-improvement bears directly on AGIRight's core themes.
doubts: Release and 15k-character section-by-section PDF read; bill text not yet published. @Miles_Brundage (2123513584441589849) says this version closes "the revenue loophole" and adds "greater specificity on IVO access"; @NatPurser (repost by Brundage and Hashim) calls the discussion draft "a significant improvement on FRONTIER 1.0" (opinions). WaPo (via @ben_guggenheim 2123499456524152858) on House Dem leadership thinking on an AI package: not opened (timeout). Topics index searched: FRONTIER+Trahan, FRONTIER Act (topics 302, 339, 346, 433, 484 are earlier federal-bill items; none on 2.0).

title: Reps. Beyer, Jacobs and Maloy release an outline of the bipartisan SAFE AI Act (Nov 19): mandatory safety frameworks, incident reporting, CAISI-assigned independent evaluators paid from fee-based funds, narrow emergency authority, civil penalties and developer liability
author_or_publisher: Offices of Reps. Don Beyer (D-VA), Sara Jacobs (D-CA) and Celeste Maloy (R-UT)
quote_verbatim: Evaluators are assigned by CAISI based on qualifications with mandatory rotations to preserve independence.
what_is_new: The outline says developers "do not pay evaluators directly", requires disclosure of substantially autonomous AI R&D, lets any person confidentially report safety incidents to CAISI, and "Clarifies liability of developers for reasonably foreseeable injuries to third parties caused by AI systems."
why_for_agiright: Bipartisan federal outline on independent evaluation, incident reporting, emergency authority and developer liability, directly on AGIRight's themes.
doubts: Outline only; legislative text "forthcoming". Rep. Jacobs's quote in the release refers to models that "break out of test environments and hack other companies’ systems" (her characterisation). @ShakeelHashim (2123489976524423513) notes Anthropic-backed Public First spent close to $1m on Maloy in her primary (see item 014). Topics index searched: SAFE AI, Beyer+Jacobs (no match).
